messages:
Maya: Heads-up — I'm opening a tiny PR to clarify the billing math for burst credits + tier attribution in the rate/usage docs. I realized the Python SDK example shows the old header name.
Alex: thanks, can you paste the snippet here? easier to review.
Maya: sure — current doc shows: `headers = {\n  'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}',\n  'X-Rate-Limit': 'tier=gold'\n}` we want to change to `X-Rw-Tier` and add a short note about fallback behavior.
Toni: is that header actually required for all customers? i thought we auto-derive tier from subscription id.
Maya: not required — only used for explicit overrides in Dedicated migrations. Added a doc sentence: "Header override only for dedicated/reserved flows; hosted customers will be derived from account mapping."
Kevin: small nit — the metrics panel queries in grafana use `sum(rate(token_consumption[5m])) by (tier)` which will break when we alias the tier label. need a one-line query update.
Sam: what should we change it to?
Kevin: change to `sum(rate(token_consumption[5m])) by (billing_tier)` and update the dashboard variable to `billing_tier`. I'll push a tiny panel change in dash repo.
Alex: also add a migration note for SDK users. i.e. `If you relied on X-Rate-Limit for tests, switch to X-Rw-Tier or remove header.` Short code sample for JS: `fetch(url,{headers:{'X-Rw-Tier':'gold'}})`
Maya: PR is #4589 — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4589 — currently WIP, includes: doc sentence, updated python/js snippets, and a table mapping old headers -> new header + reason.
Toni: can you add a unit example showing the quota calc for burst + steady state? reviewers kept asking for numbers.
Maya: added a tiny worked example: "Gold tier: base 100 req/min, burst credit 300 tokens; steady usage 120 req/min will consume 20 burst until exhausted — example calculation included."
docs-bot: auto-check — docs lint passed.
Alex: quick review done, left 2 comments about phrasing in the "fallback" paragraph.
Sam: i can take the grafana panel change after Kevin does the variable rename. we should schedule the dash deploy in the same window as the docs PR so links don't 404.
Kevin: i'll open dash PR now (#79). tagging @Sam for deploy.
Maya: thanks. Also, can we add a small note in the SDK migration guide about backcompat: show both old and new header keys and a one-liner to detect both in middleware.
Alex: yeah, example middleware snippet: `tier = req.headers['x-rw-tier'] || req.headers['x-rate-limit'] || deriveFromAccount(req)` — include that as a callout.
Toni: lgtm. one more ask: the billing analytics query example in the docs uses daily aggregation; please include a 1h example for alerting purposes.
Maya: added hourly example and an alert suggestion: `when sum(rate(token_consumption[5m])) by (billing_tier) > threshold`
Sam: can we also add a short note about how this affects the usage-export CSV? the column name will change to `billing_tier` next week. ops told me to warn customers.
Maya: added note and a small migration checklist at the bottom of the page: update SDK header, update dashboard vars, update CSV consumers.
Alex: approved once the two wording comments are addressed.
Maya: fixed wording, pushed. PR status: ready for final review.
docs-bot: PR merged by Maya — docs site will rebuild in ~10m.
Sam: i'll coordinate dash deploy after CI passes on #79. tagging @ops for release window. :thumbsup:
Kevin: dash pr merged, deploy scheduled for 03/28 02:00 UTC.
Maya: thanks all — closing thread.
